analysis: Examined three files. (1) ProviderLoop+ModelSelection.swift: adds enabledModelsAtLastSwitch, set after the persisted replacement is staged (head line 32) and restored on rollback (line 55) alongside hasPersistedModelSwitch. This is local bookkeeping that mirrors the existing persistence rollback and adds no trust-boundary change. One residual gap: if the error path throws before the restore (e.g. ownership check failure), the value stays at the new selection, which only affects recovery eligibility. (2) ProviderLoop+ModelSwitch.swift line 143: modelSwitchMutationsSettled now also requires selectedModelRecovery.attempt == nil, so the switch drain waits for an in-flight recovery load before the coordinator barrier. This is a conservative availability and ordering improvement. The recovery pause reasons (modelSwitchTask != nil, servingDrain.refusing) prevent new attempts during a switch. A small window exists between the recovery check and Task creation, but it is rechecked after the suspension (the plan sampling). No concrete race was proven. (3) New ProviderLoop+SelectedModelRecovery.swift: a capacity-tick-driven background loader for selected models left cold. It evicts only unselected, unprotected, idle models that satisfy Autopilot victim rules, rechecked before each unload, and loads with allowEviction:false. It touches no key material, attestation, encryption or coordinator wire content, and does not change what is advertised (it requires advertisedModels and ordinaryServingModelIDs membership and no failed self-test or retirement). It uses the existing ensureModelLoaded path, so weight-hash and self-test gates (T-012/T-027) should still apply, and I assumed that without seeing that code. The related threats are availability (T-029, T-016); the added eviction of unselected models is bounded by Autopilot rules. Unverified: the enqueue and prune call sites (finishStartupPreload, noteSelectedModelUnloaded) and the daemon state report schema are not in the supplied evidence. Also unverified: whether the recovery load reaches the same admission gates as request-driven loads, and whether the attempt Task is cancelled on shutdown and on switch. No findings.
